title: Redraw Credit on Mobile In-Home Collection Trips After a Specimen Rejection
content:
**Laboratory quality bulletin — Specimen Collection Appointments.** When a home trip is a redraw for an order whose specimen the laboratory rejected, the trip carries a redraw credit, which is subtracted from the trip. Rejections are read from the order's records in Laboratory Test Orders: the specimen rejection lines on the order, each with its rejection reason and date.

## The credit

- When the order's specimen was rejected **in the last three months for leaking in transit or for exceeding its stability** — failures in the laboratory's own handling — the trip carries a redraw credit of **25.00**.
- When the order's specimen was rejected in that window **only for another reason**, the credit is **10.00**.
- When **no rejection** of the order's specimen falls in that window, there is no credit.

The other rejection reasons recorded on orders are hemolyzed, quantity not sufficient, unlabeled or mislabeled, and wrong container.

## Truth table (rejections of the order's specimen in the last three months)

| Leaked in transit or stability exceeded | Another reason | Redraw credit |
|---|---|---|
| At least one | None | 25.00 |
| At least one | At least one | 25.00 |
| None | At least one | 10.00 |
| None | None | None |

## Basis Q&A

**Does a rejection five months ago count?** No; only rejections dated in the last three months count.

**Two rejections in the window, one hemolyzed and one leaked in transit?** A rejection for leaking in transit falls in the window, so the credit is 25.00; the credits do not add up.

**Is the credit tied to the patient or to the order?** To the order the visit collects; rejections on the patient's other orders are not read.
